name: CRGO Electrical Steel & Transformer Core Localisation
scope: India's import-dependent CRGO / amorphous transformer-steel supply chain, the DGTR anti-dumping probe, the JSW JFE capacity build-out, and the listed steel makers, core processors and transformer makers exposed to it.

summary.one_line: Both small-cap processors have now reported H1 FY27. Vilas's PAT fell 29% and it cut FY27 growth guidance to 30-35%. Jay Bee's PAT rose 52% but its operating cash flow was -Rs 42 cr. DGTR has still published no preliminary findings, and the processor stocks are near 52-week lows.
key_points: India uses about 400-450 kt of CRGO a year but makes only 40-50 kt, so about 90% is imported (S1). Imports of the products under investigation were worth $821.5m in FY26. China supplied 33.6% of CRGO imports, Japan 31.4%, Russia 20.6% and Korea 6.5% (S4).

DGTR opened the case (F. No. 6/17/2026-DGTR) on 22 Jun 2026 on a petition from JSW JFE Electrical Steel Nashik. It covers China, Japan, Korea and Russia, and the period of investigation is Apr 2025-Mar 2026 (S5, S39). Final findings are due within one year, extendable by six months (S26). As of 21 Nov 2026 we found no preliminary findings and no duty.

New this week: Vilas Transcore's H1 FY27 revenue rose 6.0% to Rs 242.5 cr on 28.1% higher CRGO volume (11,697 MT). EBITDA fell 20.2%, margin fell to 10.2% from 13.6%, and PAT fell 29.3% to Rs 17.2 cr because realisations were lower (S33).
Vilas cut its FY27 revenue-growth guidance to 30-35% (Rs 620-660 cr) from the 45-50% it gave in August. FY27 CRGO volume guidance is 26,000-30,000 MT (S13, S34).

New this week: Jay Bee's H1 FY27 PAT rose 52% to Rs 5.62 cr, and its EBITDA margin rose to 7.72% from 4.82%. Revenue slipped to Rs 213.0 cr from Rs 218.7 cr, with Rs 32.4 cr from new EPC work offsetting lower manufacturing sales. Operating cash flow was -Rs 42.2 cr and short-term borrowings rose to Rs 74.3 cr (S35).

The grid pull is large. The National Electricity Plan budgets Rs 9.15 lakh crore for transmission to 2032 and targets transformation capacity of 2,342 GVA, up from 1,251 GVA (S32). JSW JFE plans 350 ktpa: Vijayanagar at full output in 2027 and Nashik phased over 2028-30 (S7, S31).

The market has not re-rated the theme. Over one year, Jay Bee is -48.4% at Rs 72 (S37), Vilas -25% to -30% at Rs 302.95, near its Rs 301 52-week low (S18), and Mangal -46.3% (S38). JSW Steel, where the JV is immaterial, is +14.8% over one year (S36).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: JSW Steel, through the 50:50 JSW JFE JV. The JV is the petitioner and the only producer DGTR accepts as domestic industry (S5, S39). A duty would support pricing as Vijayanagar ramps up in 2027 and Nashik in 2028-30 (S31).

Processors with domestic sourcing, or that support the petition. ICRA notes Vilas has diversified to domestic CRGO suppliers (S12). Mangal Electrical, a 16,200 MT processor, registered with DGTR as a supporter of the domestic industry (S5, S22).

Proterial's Metglas amorphous plant at Sri City (about 30 kt/yr; 74:26 with unlisted Shirdi Sai Electricals) would supply from inside any duty wall. It was targeted to start in Oct 2026, and we found no confirmation that it has (S16).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Transformer makers that import CRGO. Indo Tech registered with DGTR as user and importer, and TARIL as importer (S5). TARIL says CRGO is 33-35% of its raw-material cost (S10). TERI estimates that a 10% CRGO price rise adds 1.5-3% to transformer cost (S11).

Processors with stretched working capital. Vilas's inventory rose to Rs 115.4 cr from Rs 72.3 cr in six months (S33). Jay Bee burned Rs 42.2 cr of operating cash in H1 and its short-term debt nearly tripled (S35). A duty-led price swing hits balance sheets like these hard.
For JSW Steel the payoff is small and late. The JV is unlisted and 50%-owned (S7), JSW booked Rs 54,486 cr of revenue in Q2 FY27 alone (S21), and most new capacity arrives in 2027-30 (S31).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: DGTR preliminary findings, if any, or the final findings due by about 22 Jun 2027 (extendable to about Dec 2027), followed by any government notification (S5, S26).
Whether Vilas delivers 26,000+ MT of CRGO volume and Rs 620-660 cr of revenue in FY27 (S34). H1 annualises to about 23.4 kt (our arithmetic, from S33).
Whether Jay Bee's operating cash flow turns positive in H2, and confirmation that Metglas Sri City has started (S35, S16).

kpis.sub: 1 yr from 22 Jun 2026, +6 mo extendable (S5, S26)

subsections.title: What CRGO and amorphous metal are

blocks.text: Cold-rolled grain-oriented (CRGO) electrical steel and amorphous metal are the core materials of power and distribution transformers. About 98% of CRGO output goes into transformers (S11). Amorphous ribbon, such as Proterial's Metglas, cuts transformer no-load losses and can reduce standby power use by about one-third compared with conventional electrical sheet (S16). The DGTR case covers both materials (S5).

The supply chain has three layers. Steel mills make the CRGO coil. Processors slit, cut and assemble it into laminations and cores: Vilas, Jay Bee, Mangal, and TARIL's POSCO Poggenamp unit. Transformer makers come last (S10, S12, S22). Estimates of CRGO's cost share differ because they use different bases. TARIL puts it at 33-35% of raw-material cost (S10). TERI puts it at 15-20% of a standard transformer's bill of materials, while an MSME source quoted 40-50% (S11).

blocks.text: BIS licensing already acts as a non-tariff gate. Imports must comply with IS 3024. In 2024, BIS licences for major Chinese exporters expired or were not renewed, which halted some shipments and caused an acute shortage, especially of Hi-B grade (S27). GTRI argues that because imports already need BIS certification, the dispute is about price, not quality (S1).

blocks.text: GTRI's case against a duty: CRGO was previously left out of safeguard duties because India depends on imports, and with domestic output under one-tenth of demand a duty mainly raises transformer and grid costs (S1). The Indian Steel Association replies that CRGO needs 7-10 times the investment per tonne of conventional steel, and that subsidised imports threaten that investment (S11). An MSME federation official says JSW is 'the only beneficiary' (S11).

Opposition is broad. DGTR's interested-party list includes the Embassy of Japan, Russia's Ministry of Economic Development, IEEMA, KOSA and the China Iron and Steel Association, plus several listed transformer makers (S5). Indian rules set no fixed deadline for preliminary findings (S26), so the timing of any interim duty is uncertain.

blocks.text: The National Electricity Plan (Transmission) budgets Rs 9.15 lakh crore to 2032. It takes the transmission network from 4.85 lakh ckm to 6.48 lakh ckm, and transformation capacity at 220 kV and above from 1,251 GVA to 2,342 GVA (S32). KNN gives a 1,290 GVA base for the same target (S11). On our arithmetic, even the full 350 ktpa from the JV plus 30 kt of amorphous ribbon is below today's 400-450 kt demand (S1, S16, S31), so imports should remain the marginal supply through 2030.

blocks.text: Falling CRGO prices, not the probe, still drive processor P&Ls. Vilas grew volume 28% but revenue only 6%, and its gross margin fell 255 bps (S33). Jay Bee's manufacturing revenue fell about 17% (our arithmetic) as material cost dropped to Rs 146.2 cr from Rs 181.2 cr, and its profit came from better margins and EPC work (S35). A duty would reverse the price trend. Processors that pass costs through would book inventory gains, and any lag would compress margins that ICRA already flags as sensitive to CRGO prices, with no formal hedging (S12). Vilas is diversifying into nanocrystalline cores, radiators and copper conductors, with conductor sales starting Sep 2026 (S33).

JSW Steel holds 50% of the JV and JFE holds the rest (S7). JSW's Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was Rs 54,486 cr and its PAT Rs 5,359 cr (S21). As an illustration only (our arithmetic, not a forecast): 350 ktpa at the Rs 190-195/kg CRGO price Vilas cited in Aug 2026 (S13) gives about Rs 6,700 cr of gross revenue for the whole JV. That is about 3% of JSW's annualised Q2 revenue before applying its 50% share, and it would build only over 2027-30 (S31).

Downstream, DGTR registrants include CG Power (user industry and exporter/producer), Hitachi Energy India, Indo Tech (user and importer), TARIL (importer), Atlanta Electricals and BHEL (S5). TARIL has partly hedged by buying 51% of POSCO Poggenamp, a 24,000 t/yr CRGO processor (S10). TERI estimates that a 10% CRGO price rise adds 1.5-3% to transformer cost, and a 20% rise adds 3-6% (S11).

items: GTRI (Ajay Srivastava): a duty raises transformer and grid costs but gives little protection, because domestic output is under one-tenth of demand (S1, S4).
TERI (Alekhya Datta): a 10% CRGO price rise adds 1.5-3% to transformer cost, and a 20% rise adds 3-6% (S11).
Indian Steel Association (Alok Sahay): domestic CRGO capacity is capital-intensive, and subsidised imports threaten investment (S11).
ICRA (Vilas, Jul 2025): [ICRA]A- (Stable)/A2+, balancing strong interest cover against working-capital intensity, customer concentration and exposure to CRGO prices (S12).
Vilas management (Nov 2026 call): about 10% EBITDA margin now and 11-12% at peak; a long-term target of Rs 1,000 cr revenue at peak utilisation (S34).

blocks.text: Coverage is still thin. This week we again found no sell-side initiation or sector note framing JSW Steel, Vilas, Jay Bee or Mangal as a CRGO localisation play. Discussion of the H1 results is limited to retail results aggregators (S33, S34, S35).

subsections.title: Has the market priced it in?

blocks.caption: Stock performance (latest dated readings found; the dashboard shows today's numbers)

blocks.title: 1-year stock return, latest reading
blocks.source: Source: 5paisa (S36, S37), Anand Rathi (S18), Value Research (S38)

blocks.text: What changed since the 7 Nov edition: after results, the processors fell further. Vilas went from Rs 338.75 to Rs 302.95, just above its Rs 301 52-week low (S18). Jay Bee went from Rs 90 to Rs 72, near its Rs 70 low, despite 52% PAT growth (S37). JSW Steel stayed near its 52-week high (S36). The probe has not re-rated the processors. The market is pricing their thin margins and cash-flow strain.

items: The duty could be rejected or diluted. Opposition is organised, including foreign governments, industry associations and large user-industry registrants (S5), and GTRI and TERI stress the cost to the grid (S1, S11).
Timing mismatch: final findings may not come until Jun-Dec 2027 (S26), while Nashik's expansion phases in only over 2028-30 (S31).
Price volatility squeezing processors. Vilas's H1 EBITDA fell 20% on 28% higher volume (S33), and Mangal's Q2 operating profit fell 29.4% (S30).

Working capital and liquidity. Jay Bee's H1 operating cash flow was -Rs 42.2 cr and its short-term debt rose to Rs 74.3 cr (S35). The market caps are tiny: Jay Bee about Rs 163 cr, Vilas about Rs 742 cr (S37, S18).
Guidance risk. Vilas has already cut its FY27 growth guidance from 45-50% to 30-35% (S13, S34).
Materiality for JSW Steel. The JV is unlisted, 50%-owned and small next to group revenue (S7, S21).

method: Weekly refresh of the 2026-W45 edition (7 Nov 2026), researched on 21 Nov 2026 with web search and direct page fetches. New this week: H1 FY27 (Sep-2026) results for Vilas (S33) and Jay Bee (S35), both from multibagg.ai summaries of the exchange filings because we did not open the original NSE PDFs; Vilas's revised FY27 guidance from an Arthneeti concall summary (S34), whose headline (20-40%) conflicts with its body (30-35% for FY27), so we use the body figure; and refreshed prices for Vilas (S18, which shows two inconsistent sets of 6-month and 1-year returns, so both are given), Jay Bee (S37), Mangal (S38, which also confirmed the NSE symbol MEIL and BSE code 544492) and JSW Steel (S36, the latest dated reading being 11 Nov). A search-result summary also cited a Vilas FY27 revenue target of Rs 750-800 cr that we could not confirm, so it is not used. We searched for DGTR preliminary findings, a Metglas Sri City start and new JSW JFE announcements and found none dated after the last edition. Dropped as superseded: the Value Research Jay Bee page and the 3 Nov JSW price (S19, S29), the multibagg Jay Bee FY26 piece (S14), the duplicate Machine Maker capex article (S8), the Mondaq note (S6, replaced by World Trade Scanner S39 for the POI and retrospective-duty request) and the PL Capital note (S28). Carried-forward figures (GTRI balance, import mix, JV capex, ICRA, TARIL, TERI, the DGTR interested-party list) come from previously fetched sources. We found no other listed CRGO steel maker: NLMK India and Shirdi Sai Electricals appear unlisted, and DGTR excludes NLMK from domestic industry. Producer coverage is therefore JSW Steel alone, which is the honest state of this niche. Voltamp and Shilchar were again left out for lack of a citable CRGO link. Revenue and utilisation arithmetic is our own and labelled as such. No ratings or price targets. Source IDs are not contiguous.
